newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dubai-based Dolphin seals S.Africa parks deal.
newsitem.headline: Dubai-based Dolphin seals S.Africa parks deal.

text.p: A revised deal giving Dubai-based Dolphin Group commercial control over nature reserves in South Africa's northeastern Mpumalanga province was ratified on Wednesday, the firm said.

Dolphin said in a statement the new deal, which replaced an original agreement which came under heavy fire from environmental groups, was unanimously agreed by a meeting of the Mpumalanga Parks Board.
An original 50-year lease has been shortened to 25 years and the firm has agreed to invest 410 million rand ($92.8 million) in the project over three years.

"Dolphin is committed to working closely with the local communities in the region to ensure that they are fully involved in all of the developments and reap the benefits of the projects to the greatest extent," said Dolphin chief executive Ketan Somaia.
Two areas, one a nature reserve and the other a historic mining town, are excluded under the new terms negotiated in London by Somaia and a delegation of South Africans.
The agreement still faces the problem of land claims lodged by black communities living near the reserves who say their territory was taken from them under apartheid.

Dolphin has offered black communities on the borders of the reserves a 20 percent share of the development companies, but has left the politically sensitive claims to be handled by the Mpumalanga Parks Board.
The reserves are all in Mpumalanga province, also the site of the Kruger National Park, a reserve roughly the same size as Israel, but which is excluded from the agreement.

Environmental activists slammed the original deal, which was signed without any public debate. They charged the board with giving too much power to Dolphin and of selling off some of the country's environmental crown jewels.

However, a Parks Board official said the way was now clear for the deal to go ahead. "There is a great deal of hard work ahead of us and our starting point is to focus on communications with the communities which will be involved," he said.
